question: A 56-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination one week after a chest x-ray showed a solitary pulmonary nodule. He has no history of major medical illness. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 30 years. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. A tuberculin skin test is negative. A CT scan of the chest shows a 2.1-cm well-circumscribed, calcified nodule in the periphery of the right lower lung field. A CT-guided biopsy of the lesion is performed. Histological examination of the biopsy specimen shows regions of disorganized hyaline cartilage interspersed with myxoid regions and clefts of ciliated epithelium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "56-year-old man with solitary pulmonary nodule" -> "History of smoking increases lung cancer risk" -> "CT shows well-circumscribed, calcified nodule" -> "Histology shows disorganized hyaline cartilage" -> "Presence of myxoid regions and ciliated epithelium" -> "Features consistent with pulmonary hamartoma" -> 85%

CHAIN: "56-year-old man with solitary pulmonary nodule" -> "Negative tuberculin skin test suggests no active tuberculosis" -> "CT shows 2.1-cm calcified nodule" -> "Histological examination reveals cartilage and epithelium" -> "Findings not typical for malignancy" -> "Most likely diagnosis is pulmonary hamartoma" -> 90%

CHAIN: "56-year-old man with solitary pulmonary nodule" -> "Smoking history raises suspicion for lung pathology" -> "CT shows well-defined calcified nodule" -> "Biopsy shows hyaline cartilage and myxoid areas" -> "Ciliated epithelium present indicates benign nature" -> "Diagnosis of pulmonary hamartoma is likely" -> 80%

CHAIN: "56-year-old man with solitary pulmonary nodule" -> "Calcified nodule suggests a benign process" -> "Histology shows cartilage and myxoid regions" -> "Ciliated epithelium indicates a non-malignant lesion" -> "Pulmonary hamartoma is a strong possibility" -> 75%
analysis: The histological examination shows regions of disorganized hyaline cartilage, myxoid regions, and clefts of ciliated epithelium, which are characteristic features of a pulmonary hamartoma. This benign tumor is often calcified and typically presents as a well-circumscribed nodule on imaging. The patient's smoking history and the solitary nature of the nodule further support this diagnosis, as pulmonary hamartomas are the most common benign lung tumors and can occur in smokers.
